post.description:
Ask a question and get an answer that an OpenAI model wrote after searching the live web. Send a Responses request — an `input` string (or message array) — and the endpoint injects a fixed, server-pinned model and the `web_search` tool for you; the model, tool and per-request search cap are server-controlled to keep cost bounded. The reply is a standard OpenAI Responses object: `output[]` contains `web_search_call` items (each a search that ran) and a `message` item with the answer text and URL citations, and the billed search count equals the number of `web_search_call` items.  Use this when you want a written, cited answer grounded in current web content from an OpenAI model — for the Anthropic-model equivalent see [`post_anthropic_websearch_search`](/api-reference/search/post_anthropic-websearch-search), and for raw ranked links with extracted page text use [`post_tavily_search`](/api-reference/search/post_tavily-search).

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->
Usage-based billing; Default request estimate: $0.3 USD (not a fixed price). Account-specific pricing and final settlement may differ.
<!-- aisa-pricing:end -->

example.input: What are the three biggest AI announcements this week? Give one sentence each with sources.

input.description: Your question or instruction, same format as the OpenAI Responses API `input`. A message array is also accepted.
input.example: What are the three biggest AI announcements this week? Give one sentence each with sources.

instructions.description: Optional high-level instructions to steer the answer's tone or format.

max_output_tokens.description: Optional cap on the number of tokens generated in the answer.

output.description: Ordered items: web_search_call (searches performed) and message (the cited answer).

200.description: A standard OpenAI Responses object. `output[]` interleaves web_search_call items and the cited answer message; the number of web_search_call items is the billed search count.

default.description: Error response; upstream passthrough responses may use provider formats

x-codeSamples.source:
# Fixed reference example. Playground inputs do not update this sample.
curl --request POST \
  --url https://dev-api.aisa.one/apis/v1/openai-websearch/search \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "input": "What are the three biggest AI announcements this week? Give one sentence each with sources.",
  "max_output_tokens": 1024
}'
